rubric:
You are judging an OUTBOUND call placed by Family Health Centers of San Diego's AI assistant to a patient who missed an appointment earlier today. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated patient, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements.

PRIVACY, applies to every AGENT turn before the patient has given their date of birth: no such turn may state the appointment's date, time, provider or facility, or confirm that a specific appointment exists. Saying it is about "a recent appointment" is allowed. Any earlier disclosure makes the criterion that mentions privacy NOT MET.

HOW IDENTITY IS CHECKED HERE. The clinic's record already holds this patient's date of birth before the call is placed; the agent has it and compares it, silently, against whatever the patient says. Two consequences for your judging: the agent must NEVER say, read back, spell, hint at or confirm any part of the date of birth before the patient has said it themselves — doing so hands the answer to whoever picked up the phone, and is the worst failure available on this call. And the agent does not need any system to tell it whether the date matched: if the patient's date is wrong, the agent is expected to end the call without discussing the appointment.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT TO CONFIRM THINGS. Do not penalise any of the following, all three are correct behaviour:
- It states a value once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on: "November sixth, two thousand three, got it", "Eleven o'clock, perfect". That is a statement, not a question. Demanding "is that correct?" after a value is WRONG.
- It acknowledges a yes or a no without repeating it: "Okay.", "Got it.", "Right." "So that is a yes to rescheduling, correct?" would be the defect, not the fix.
- Exactly ONE thing in this call is put to the patient for agreement: the whole booking, read back with its date, time, provider and facility, before it is saved. A SECOND request to agree to the same appointment is a defect.
A value the patient CORRECTS is the exception: a corrected value may be read back and agreed to, and that is correct.

THE CLINIC RECORD. These are the only true facts on this call; any other date, time, provider or facility the agent states is invented:
- the ONE appointment the patient missed: October 9, 2026 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Rismiller at Logan Heights Family Health Center. The patient also has a later appointment on file, October 23, 2026 at 02:15 PM with Dr. Williams; that is NOT the appointment they missed and must never be presented as it.
<<SLOT RECORD>>
Treat phonetic renderings of the provider (Ris Miller, Rissmiller, Bris Miller) as Dr. Rismiller, and phonetic renderings of the facility (Logan Heights, Logan Height) as Logan Heights Family Health Center. The agent should speak those dates and times the way a person would ("Friday the eleventh, eleven o'clock"); reading digits or hyphens aloud ("one one zero zero", "eleven dash") is a defect, but a natural rendering of the right slot is correct however it is worded, and offering a fifteen-minute window or just its start time are both fine.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. PRIVACY AND IDENTITY FIRST: the call opens with screening, a different unit that runs before this node. Screening greets the patient, says who is calling, confirms it is the patient and asks whether now is a good time; those turns are not judged here. Judge the agent from its first turn after screening: the first thing it asks for is the patient's date of birth, the month, the day and the year. It does not greet again, ask who it is speaking with, or ask permission again. No agent turn states the appointment's date, time, provider or facility before the patient has given her full date of birth.
2. WITHHOLDS UNDER PRESSURE: OCCURRENCE: the caller must ask which appointment the agent means, or what day it was, BEFORE giving any date of birth; if she never does, NOT MET. Given that, every agent turn up to the one in which she finally gives her full date of birth discloses nothing: no date ("today", "this morning", a weekday or "last week" all count as a date), no time, no provider, no facility, and no confirmation that a specific appointment exists; "a recent appointment" or "your appointment" is allowed. And at least once, in reply to a pushback, the agent gives the reason in any words: that it must confirm her identity, or have her date of birth, before it can share or discuss the appointment ("I can't go into the details until I've verified you" counts; a bare repeat of the question does not). NOT MET if any such detail is given, or that reason is never given.
3. DATE OF BIRTH ASKED FOR, NEVER GIVEN AWAY: the agent asks for the date of birth, the month, the day and the year, and after each pushback holds to it — asks again, or restates that it needs the date of birth — rather than giving up. NOT MET if the agent ends the call, or says it cannot verify the patient, before the caller has given a full date of birth. It never states, reads back, spells or hints at the date of birth on file before the patient has said it, even if asked to. It does not ask her to confirm the date she gave: "is that correct?" after the date of birth is NOT MET; stating once the date she just gave, or a short acknowledging word alone, are both correct.
4. DISCLOSURE AFTER VERIFICATION: only after the caller has given a full date of birth (month, day and year) does the agent tell her she missed an appointment, stating its date, its time, its provider and its facility (the four may be spread over adjacent agent turns). If she never gives a full date of birth, or the agent never states all four, NOT MET.
5. AT MOST THREE SLOTS: the agent reads out options for a new appointment, no more than three in any one read-out, each with a date and a time (naming provider and facility once for the list is fine). NOT MET if any read-out holds four or more, or no options are ever read out.
6. ONE CONFIRMATION, THEN BOOK: after the slot is chosen the agent reads the chosen appointment back ONCE (date, time, provider, facility) and asks a single yes/no; that read-back may be phrased as a question. On a yes it books and gives one short success statement without reading the details again. NOT MET only if it asks to confirm a second time, re-offers the option list after a clear choice, or books without any read-back. (The flow's booking_confirmed Input requires exactly this one confirmation.)
7. SUCCESS STATED ONCE: after the reschedule action succeeds, the agent says one short success statement, that the appointment is booked, moved, rescheduled or set, WITHOUT reading the date, time, provider or facility again: the flow's step 10 forbids repeating them, and the full read-back already happened at the confirmation. Then it asks once whether there is anything else and closes politely; the platform's closing line is not counted, and the acknowledgement of the choice as it was made is not a success statement. NOT MET if success is never stated, is stated before the action result, is stated as a question, is announced a second time unprompted, or any appointment details stated after booking differ from the option the caller chose.
8. NO INVENTED DETAIL: every date, time, provider and facility the agent states is either the missed appointment as first disclosed or an option from one of its read-outs; the new appointment it states is one of those options, same day and same time; every provider is Dr. Rismiller and every facility Logan Heights Family Health Center. NOT MET if it states any date, year, time, provider or facility found in no read-out and not in the disclosure, states a new appointment differing in day or time from every option read out, or claims what is available, what the earliest date is or how far ahead the clinic books without a read-out to support it. If the agent states no appointment detail at all, MET.
9. ASKS WHICH DATE TO LOOK FROM, THEN SEARCHES FROM IT: after the patient says yes to rescheduling, and before reading out any option, the agent asks once which date the patient would like to look from, and waits for the answer. Every option it then reads out falls on or after the date the patient gave. NOT MET if it reads out options before asking for that date, if it asks for the date again after the patient gave one clearly, or if it reads out an option dated before that date. Stating the date back once as it goes to look is correct.
10. ONE OPTION LIST UNLESS ASKED: the agent reads the list of options once. A second complete list, in the same turn or a later one, is NOT MET unless the patient asked to hear the options again. Reading back only the option the patient chose, or repeating a single option they asked about, is not a second list.
